title: Five big squares without long multiplication
description: Each of five numbers is split into a round number and a small one, and the square is built from three parts by the rule for a sum squared or a take away squared. The board puts each answer back by its last digit.
teaching_notes: One idea: split the number near a round number, then use the sum squared rule or the take away squared rule. Watch for students who leave out the middle part, twice the two parts multiplied.

source: Figure it Out (squares and patterns, question 3)
video_script.why: The child knows the two square rules, but has not yet chosen a round number to split a larger number around.
video_script.substitution: Split each number near a round number, and use the sum squared rule or the take away squared rule, as the examples in the book did.
video_script.anchor: the five numbers of the book's question, each ready to be split
video_script.payoff_line: The last square, one hundred twenty four squared, is fifteen thousand three hundred seventy six.

final_answer.spoken: one hundred sixty four thousand eight hundred thirty six, five thousand one hundred eighty four, twenty one thousand twenty five, one million two hundred three thousand four hundred nine, fifteen thousand three hundred seventy six

maths_rules: last digits: 6×6 = 36 ends in 6; 2×2 = 4; 5×5 = 25 ends in 5; 7×7 = 49 ends in 9; 4×4 = 16 ends in 6
video_script.design: One idea: split near a round number and build the square from three parts. Both rule cards stay on the stage, and the last square is left unadded until the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Your book gave two rules. A sum squared is eigh squared plus two eigh b plus b squared.
<bookmark mark='take'/>A take away squared is eigh squared minus two eigh b plus b squared.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five numbers to square.

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, split four hundred six as four hundred plus six. Four hundred squared is one hundred sixty thousand.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice four hundred times six is four thousand eight hundred. Six squared is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Adding the three parts, four hundred six squared is one hundred sixty four thousand eight hundred thirty six.
<bookmark mark='split2'/>Split seventy two as seventy plus two. Seventy squared is four thousand nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='mid2'/>Twice seventy times two is two hundred eighty. Two squared is four.
<bookmark mark='sum2'/>Adding, seventy two squared is five thousand one hundred eighty four.

marks.mid2: the middle part 6600 and the last part 9 appear
marks.sum2: the middle part is taken away to give 1203409

beats.colours: the three terms in three colours
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, split one hundred forty five as one hundred fifty minus five. One hundred fifty squared is twenty two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice one hundred fifty times five is one thousand five hundred. Five squared is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Taking away the middle part, one hundred forty five squared is twenty one thousand twenty five.
<bookmark mark='split2'/>Split one thousand ninety seven as one thousand one hundred minus three. One thousand one hundred squared is one million two hundred ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='mid2'/>Twice one thousand one hundred times three is six thousand six hundred. Three squared is nine.
<bookmark mark='sum2'/>Taking away the middle part, the square is one million two hundred three thousand four hundred nine.

marks.parts: the three parts 14400, 960 and 16 appear, not yet added

beats.colours: the three terms in three colours
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, split one hundred twenty four as one hundred twenty plus four.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>One hundred twenty squared is fourteen thousand four hundred. Twice one hundred twenty times four is nine hundred sixty. Four squared is sixteen.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step four, put the answers back against the question, by the last digit. Six times six is thirty six, so the first square ends in six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Two times two is four, so the second ends in four.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Five times five is twenty five, so the third ends in five.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>Seven times seven is forty nine, so the fourth ends in nine.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>Four times four is sixteen, so the last square must end in six.
